small_guidance:
- Switch BLOCK_OC=128, BLOCK_SP=16 (so SP_FULL=64) and BLOCK_IC=32 to better fit tl.dot tile shapes (128×32 × 32×64) — current 64×16×128 is K-thin which underutilizes tensor cores. Try num_warps=4 with num_stages=2 as well.
- Wrap the launch in `triton.autotune` over {BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_SP, BLOCK_IC, num_warps, num_stages} with 4-6 configs keyed on (OC, POH*POW, IC).
- Hoist the `pid_n * IC*IH*IW` base offset and precompute `sp_in_off` once outside the IC loop (currently it's recomputed each kh,kw iteration but inside the IC loop body — move x_off base computation out of the IC loop to reduce index arithmetic).
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an explicit im2col GEMM: collapse (KH,KW,IC) into the K dimension and (POOL*POOL within a pooled tile) into the M (or N) dimension so the inner loop is a single GEMM-K reduction with one tl.dot per K-block, instead of a 9× outer static loop over (kh,kw) each issuing its own dot. This raises arithmetic intensity per dot and lets Triton pipeline loads better.
- Use a channels-last (NHWC) input layout — permute x and weight once in forward — so the GEMM-K (IC) axis is contiguous in memory, making the inner tl.load fully coalesced rather than strided by IH*IW.
- Make the kernel persistent over (N, OC-tile): one program iterates the pooled-spatial tiles, amortizing weight loads across many output positions for the same OC block. Combined with the larger M tile from POOL*POOL fusion, this should push closer to the cuDNN baseline.
